title: Deveria ter, poderia ter
theme: Modal perfects (should have, could have, would have, might have, must have done)
goal: Student uses modal perfects to speculate about the past, express regret, criticism, or strong inference.
connects_to: M15 (Passive intro) — shift from speculation about past to passive voice basics.

units.title: I should have
units.grammar_focus: should have / shouldn't have + past participle (regret + criticism)
units.real_life_context: You criticize past decisions — your own or others' — or express regret.

grammar.sentence: I _____ studied harder for the exam.
grammar.explanation: "Should have + past participle" expressa arrependimento ou crítica sobre o passado. "I should have studied" — não estudei, e foi um erro.

grammar.sentence: You _____ told her the truth.
grammar.explanation: "You should have told her" — crítica/sugestão retrospectiva. Era a coisa certa a fazer mas não foi feita.

grammar.sentence: She _____ said anything — it wasn't her business.
grammar.explanation: "Shouldn't have + past participle" para criticar uma ação passada errada. "She shouldn't have said" — disse e foi errado.

grammar.sentence: We _____ left earlier — we missed the train.
grammar.explanation: "We should have left earlier" — arrependimento sobre timing passado.

grammar.sentence: He _____ have apologized.
grammar.explanation: "He should have apologized" — sugestão retrospectiva: era a coisa correta. (Aceita "should" no contexto criticando que ele não pediu desculpa.)

grammar.sentence: I _____ have eaten so much.
grammar.explanation: "I shouldn't have eaten so much" — comi demais, me arrependo.

grammar.sentence: You _____ have called me first.
grammar.explanation: "You should have called me first" — crítica leve sobre não ter ligado.

grammar.sentence: I should studied harder.
grammar.explanation: "Should studied" não existe. Sempre "should HAVE + past participle". Forma fixa.

grammar.sentence: She shouldn't said that.
grammar.explanation: "Shouldn't have + past participle". "Shouldn't said" não é gramatical.

grammar.passage: I should have studied harder. You should have told her the truth. We shouldn't have eaten so much. He should have apologized when he had the chance.
grammar.question: What does the speaker think they should have done?
grammar.explanation: The text says "I should have studied harder".

listening_speaking.text: We shouldn't have left so late.

units.title: I could have
units.grammar_focus: could have / couldn't have + past participle (past possibility/missed chance)
units.real_life_context: You talk about missed past opportunities or impossibilities.

grammar.sentence: I _____ called you yesterday but I forgot.
grammar.explanation: "Could have + past participle" = possibilidade passada não realizada. "I could have called" — tinha como mas não chamei.

grammar.sentence: She _____ won the race, but she fell.
grammar.explanation: "She could have won" — capacidade passada, oportunidade perdida.

grammar.sentence: We _____ stayed longer, but we were tired.
grammar.explanation: "Could have stayed" — possibilidade passada, decisão de não fazer.

grammar.sentence: He _____ done it alone — he didn't need help.
grammar.explanation: "He could have done it alone" — capacidade real existia, oportunidade existia.

grammar.sentence: You _____ asked me — I would have helped.
grammar.explanation: "You could have asked me" — chance que existia mas não foi usada.

grammar.sentence: I _____ have gone, but I chose to stay.
grammar.explanation: "I could have gone" — possibilidade existia, decisão de não fazer.

grammar.sentence: She _____ have known — she wasn't even there.
grammar.explanation: "She couldn't have known" — impossibilidade lógica passada. Não tinha como saber.

grammar.sentence: I could called you but I forgot.
grammar.answer: I could have called you but I forgot.
grammar.explanation: "Could called" não existe. Sempre "could HAVE + past participle".

grammar.sentence: She couldn't known about it.
grammar.answer: She couldn't have known about it.
grammar.explanation: "Couldn't have + past participle". Sem "have", a frase é incorreta.

grammar.passage: I could have called you yesterday but I forgot. She could have won the race if she hadn't fallen. He couldn't have known about the meeting — he was on vacation.
grammar.question: Why couldn't he have known about the meeting?
grammar.explanation: The text says "He couldn't have known about the meeting — he was on vacation".

units.title: Must have / Can't have
units.grammar_focus: must have / can't have + past participle (strong inference about past)
units.real_life_context: You make confident guesses about what happened based on evidence.

grammar.sentence: She isn't answering — she _____ left already.
grammar.explanation: "Must have + past participle" = inferência forte sobre o passado. Evidência (não atende) → conclusão forte (já saiu).

grammar.sentence: He _____ stolen it — he was with me all day!
grammar.explanation: "Can't have + past participle" = impossibilidade lógica baseada em evidência. Estava comigo → impossível ter roubado.

grammar.sentence: The grass is wet — it _____ rained last night.
grammar.explanation: Evidência física (grama molhada) → conclusão forte ("must have rained").

grammar.sentence: She _____ heard you — she had headphones on.
grammar.explanation: "Can't have heard" = impossível ter ouvido (headphones). Inferência negativa forte.

grammar.sentence: He looks tired — he _____ slept much last night.
grammar.explanation: Tired → can't have slept much. Conclusão forte negativa.

grammar.sentence: They _____ enjoyed the trip — they have so many photos!
grammar.explanation: Muitas fotos → must have enjoyed. Evidência → inferência positiva forte.

grammar.sentence: She _____ have arrived — her car isn't here.
grammar.explanation: "She can't have arrived" — sem carro = não chegou. Inferência negativa.

grammar.sentence: She must left already — she's not answering.
grammar.answer: She must have left already — she's not answering.
grammar.explanation: "Must left" não existe. Sempre "must HAVE + past participle".

grammar.sentence: He can't stole it — he was with me!
grammar.answer: He can't have stolen it — he was with me!
grammar.explanation: "Can't HAVE + past participle". E note: stolen, não stole, como past participle.

grammar.passage: The grass is wet — it must have rained last night. She isn't answering her phone — she must have left already. He can't have stolen it — he was with me the whole day.
grammar.question: Why couldn't he have stolen it?
grammar.answer: he was with me (or "he was with the speaker the whole day")
grammar.explanation: The text says "He can't have stolen it — he was with me the whole day".

units.title: Might have / Needn't have
units.grammar_focus: might have + past participle (uncertainty); needn't have + past participle (unnecessary done action)
units.real_life_context: You speculate with uncertainty about the past, or notice actions that weren't needed.

grammar.sentence: She _____ missed the bus — I'm not sure.
grammar.explanation: "Might have + past participle" = especulação fraca, possibilidade incerta. Sem evidência forte.

grammar.sentence: We _____ booked the table — it was empty anyway.
grammar.explanation: "Needn't have + past participle" = ação foi feita mas não era necessária. Booked = fizemos, mas não precisava.

grammar.sentence: He _____ called — but I'm not certain.
grammar.explanation: "Might have called" — possibilidade fraca, incerteza.

grammar.sentence: You _____ brought a gift — it wasn't expected.
grammar.explanation: "Needn't have brought" — você trouxe mas não precisava. Ação desnecessária.

grammar.sentence: They _____ have left already.
grammar.explanation: "They might have left" — possibilidade incerta. Talvez sim, talvez não.

grammar.sentence: I _____ have worried so much — everything turned out fine.
grammar.explanation: "I needn't have worried" — me preocupei mas não precisava. Crítica retrospectiva à própria ação.

grammar.sentence: She _____ have forgotten — let me text her.
grammar.explanation: "She might have forgotten" — incerteza positiva. Pode ter esquecido.

grammar.sentence: She might forgotten about the meeting.
grammar.answer: She might have forgotten about the meeting.
grammar.explanation: Sempre "might HAVE + past participle". "Might forgotten" é incorreto.

grammar.sentence: You needn't brought a gift.
grammar.answer: You needn't have brought a gift.
grammar.explanation: "Needn't HAVE + past participle". "Needn't brought" é incorreto.

grammar.passage: She might have missed the bus — let me check. We needn't have booked the table — it was empty anyway. You needn't have brought a gift, but thank you.
grammar.question: Why didn't they need to book the table?
grammar.answer: it was empty (or "it was empty anyway")
grammar.explanation: The text says "We needn't have booked the table — it was empty anyway".

listening_speaking.text: She might have missed the bus.
You needn't have come — but thanks.

grammar.sentence: I _____ called you sooner — I'm sorry.
grammar.explanation: "Should have called" — arrependimento/desculpa retrospectiva.

grammar.sentence: He _____ left already — he's not here.
grammar.explanation: Evidência (não está aqui) → inferência forte ("must have left").

grammar.sentence: We _____ stayed — it ended early.
grammar.explanation: "Needn't have stayed" — ficamos mas não precisava. Ação desnecessária.

grammar.sentence: She _____ heard us — she had headphones on.
grammar.explanation: "Can't have heard" — impossibilidade lógica (headphones).

grammar.sentence: You _____ have asked — I would have helped.
grammar.explanation: "Could have asked" — oportunidade que existia.

grammar.sentence: They _____ have left already — but I'm not sure.
grammar.explanation: "Might have left" — especulação incerta.

grammar.sentence: I _____ have spoken so loudly — sorry.
grammar.explanation: "Shouldn't have spoken so loudly" — arrependimento de ação passada.

grammar.sentence: She must left already.
grammar.explanation: Sempre modal + HAVE + past participle. "Must left" não existe.

grammar.sentence: You shouldn't said that.
grammar.explanation: "Shouldn't have + past participle". Forma fixa.

grammar.passage: I should have called you sooner. She must have left already. He can't have known about it. We needn't have rushed — there was plenty of time. You could have asked me for help.
grammar.question: Why didn't they need to rush?
grammar.explanation: The text says "We needn't have rushed — there was plenty of time".
